mechanism: Loperamide slows intestinal motility and can reduce potassium absorption, while also increasing risk of hyperkalemia through reduced fecal elimination in patients with underlying renal impairment or those taking potassium supplements.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels in patients on chronic loperamide therapy, especially with potassium supplementation; consider alternative antidiarrheals if hyperkalemia develops or in renal-compromised patients.
